blocks.text: Dear Ms. Herrera:

This letter records the terms on which our firm will work with {{fact:f:E-2023-001.client}} on the executive messaging we discussed, and it becomes our agreement once you have signed and returned it. We have set it down in plain terms, so that it reads as a fair account of that conversation rather than as a document to be decoded.
Please read it alongside what we talked through. If any line here sits differently from how you understood it, say so before you sign, and we will put it right together.
What We Will Do

We will help {{fact:f:E-2023-001.client}} settle on a clear and steady account of its leadership for the audiences whose reading of the company counts most, and give your executives language they can carry into announcements, briefings, and the ordinary run of investor conversation. Our concern is that what is already true of the company is heard plainly by the people who need to hear it, and that the account holds its shape wherever it is repeated.

In practice this covers the core executive messages and the narrative that frames them, the written materials that carry those messages outward, and our counsel through the moments over the term that will test them. It does not reach into the running of the company or into decisions that are properly yours; where our advice touches those, it stays advice, and the call remains with you.
How We Work

Our method is unhurried and, we hope, plain in feel. We begin by listening, to your leadership and to the people inside and outside the company who already hold a view of it, and we set a small number of core messages down in writing before we build anything on top of them.

From there we prepare the materials that carry those messages and stay close through the moments that put them to work. When circumstances shift over the roughly five months ahead, and they will, we come back to you and adjust the account with you, and not around you.

Because so much of this work lives in correspondence, we keep a clear record of what we send and route anything client-facing through a single point on each side. You will always know what has changed and what is still open, and you will never have to hunt for the current version.
Who Will Do the Work

John Macias will carry the engagement day to day and will be your first point of contact for anything of substance. He does the close work on the drafts and keeps the moving parts legible, and he is the person to bring a question to when it needs a quick answer.

Amy Carter will support the drafting and coordination and keep our correspondence with you in good order, so that where a thread stands is always clear to whoever picks it up next. I will keep a hand on the work myself, particularly on the sensitive announcements, and nothing of weight will leave our office under our name without my having read it. You are welcome to come to me directly at any point, though John Macias will usually be the faster route to an answer.
Fees and Payment

Our fee for the engagement is {{fact:f:E-2023-001.fee}}, covering the work described above through its expected close. We will invoice against that amount as the work proceeds, and our invoices are payable within thirty days of receipt.

The fee covers our people and their time. It does not cover out-of-pocket costs such as travel, print production, or third-party services, which we will agree with you before anything of consequence is incurred. Should the shape of the work change materially, we will raise the fee with you and settle it before that work begins.
Term and Notice
The engagement begins {{fact:f:E-2023-001.start}} and is expected to run for about five months. We will treat it as finished when the work is genuinely done rather than when the calendar says so.

Either of us may bring it to a close on fourteen days' written notice. If you end it, you will owe us for work properly completed to that point and for costs already committed on your behalf, and nothing beyond that.
Confidentiality

Everything we learn about {{fact:f:E-2023-001.client}} in the course of the work we will hold in confidence and use only for the engagement. That obligation binds our whole team, survives the end of our work together, and covers the fact of our involvement as much as its substance. We ask the same of you for the methods and materials we share with you.
Limitation of Liability

We will do the work with the care and skill you are entitled to expect, and we stand behind it. We do not, though, control how the press, the markets, or other third parties will finally respond, and so our liability to you under this engagement is limited to the fees paid under it, except where the law does not permit such a limit.
Governing Law

This agreement is governed by the law of the state in which our firm is established, and any dispute under it will be resolved in that state's courts. If any single provision is found unenforceable, the remainder of this letter stands unaffected.

If this reflects our understanding, please sign and return one copy and keep the other for your records. Once it is back with us, John Macias will be in touch to arrange the first conversations, and we can set the kickoff from there. We are glad to be working with the Suarez-Jones team.

We are under way on the executive messaging work for {{fact:f:E-2023-001.client}}, with our start set at {{fact:f:E-2023-001.start}}. The aim is a clear, steady account of the company's leadership for the audiences that matter to it, and language the executives can carry into their announcements and investor conversations. This memo sets out how the work divides and what each of us picks up first, so no one waits on a hand-off that was never made.

A word first on how we will keep it in order. We hold the messaging small and written down early, we route everything client-facing through one contact, and we log what we send so the record stays clean as the volume grows. None of that is new to us, but it is worth saying once at the start.
How the work divides

items: Discovery. John Macias runs the opening interviews with the company's leadership and the people around them, and brings back what we hear in a form the rest of us can use.
Core messaging. Amy Carter turns the discovery into a first set of written messages, kept small enough to hold and to repeat without drift.
Materials and turnaround. Julie Bailey takes the agreed messages into the client-facing drafts and turns edits quickly when the copy needs to be clean and out the door.
Client coordination. Jennifer Herrera is our point of contact at Suarez-Jones; approvals and scheduling on their side run through her, and we keep her copied on anything that touches timing.

blocks.text: Two things to hold in mind as we start. Jennifer Herrera has asked that we keep the leadership close to the drafts, so plan for a round of review with the executives before anything is final; and because this messaging will surface in announcements, we weigh the sensitive lines twice before they leave the office.
First steps

items: 1. John Macias books the kickoff call with Jennifer Herrera this week and sends the invite round to the team.
2. Amy Carter drafts the messaging outline from the kickoff conversation, so we have something concrete to react to rather than a blank page.
3. Julie Bailey opens the materials folder and the correspondence file, so nothing we produce lives only in an inbox.
4. Everyone sends me their availability for the kickoff by Wednesday, so I can offer Jennifer Herrera two or three firm windows.

blocks.text: The first thing that has to happen is the kickoff call, and the rest keys off the date it sets. Send me anything you want raised there by the end of the week, and flag now anything you are unsure of, so we settle it before we sit down with the client.
Good morning Jennifer,

I am opening this thread so our notes on the executive messaging work for {{fact:f:E-2023-001.client}} stay in one place as we get going. For your file and ours, the working contacts are set: Jennifer Herrera on your side, and on ours Amy Carter, who is drafting the core messages, with me carrying the engagement day to day.

We have made a start on the Suarez-Jones messaging. We are pulling together the list for the opening interviews, and Amy Carter is shaping the first set of executive messages from what we heard at the kickoff. You will hear from us on a steady cadence from here, and each note will be tied to the piece of work it concerns, so the thread stays easy to follow.

One thing would help before we get much further: your read on which audience comes first for the leadership story. If the investor view and the internal view pull in different directions, tell me now and we will build to it. A short call works if that is easier than writing it out, and I will set one up on your word.
Regards
Jennifer,

Picking up John Macias's note, I have the first set of executive messages for {{fact:f:E-2023-001.client}} in draft and will have it to you by the end of the week. It follows the frame from the kickoff, so it should read in the company's own voice rather than ours.

On the audience question John raised, my instinct is to lead with the investor view and let the internal story follow from it, but I would rather have your read before the wording sets. The two are close enough here that a short conversation would likely settle it.
For the file, final sign-off on the Suarez-Jones messaging stays with you, Jennifer Herrera. Send the draft back with anything marked and I will turn it the same day.
Regards
Good morning Jennifer,

Thank you both. To bring the timing together in one place: Amy Carter will have the first set of executive messages for {{fact:f:E-2023-001.client}} to you by the end of the week, and I will hold a short window early next week for us to walk through it together.

On which audience leads, I would rather settle it with you on that call than guess at it now, so the wording sets around your view and not ours. If it helps, I will send two or three possible times this afternoon.

In the meantime, if anyone else on the Suarez-Jones side should see the draft before it is final, let me know and we will get it in front of them. I have you, Jennifer Herrera, as our approver on the final wording, so nothing goes out without your sign-off. I will follow up with those call windows shortly.
Regards
Jennifer,

Following John Macias's note, the first set of {{fact:f:E-2023-001.client}} executive messages will be with you tomorrow, a day ahead of where we landed, so you have it in hand before the call next week.

I have kept the draft close to how the company already speaks, so it reads in your voice rather than ours, and I have flagged the two or three lines where the audience question changes the wording. Those are the places your read will matter most.

Sign-off on the final wording sits with you, Jennifer Herrera. Mark any changes straight onto the draft when it arrives and send it back, and I will turn them the same day so the Suarez-Jones messaging is ready to walk through on the call.
Regards
